overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the March 31 notice topic naming the Chief Human Resource Officer appointment was sufficiently specific, and the AG declined to review the committee-referral allegation as outside its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Notice topic confirming a named appointee as Chief Human Resource Officer allegedly lacked salary, contract length, and start/end dates.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that where the notice informed the public that the Council would be discussing the appointment of a Chief Human Resource Officer, and that is in fact what it discussed, the notice was sufficient to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Allegation that the Council did not refer the appointment to the Human Resources Committee as it had voted to do at an earlier meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we therefore decline to review allegations that, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
